sights.n: United Temple (United Five Temples of Toa Payoh)
sights.w: Established 1974, the first temple in Singapore to house smaller constituent temples under one roof — five village temples (Chee Tian Keng, Shan Zu Yuan Fu De Ci, Tong Xing Gang, Zhao Ying Ci and others) that were displaced when Toa Payoh's kampongs were cleared pooled their devotees' funds to build here. A landmark on NHB's Toa Payoh Heritage Trail 'Of Faiths & Beliefs' route.

A Dravidian-style Hindu temple to the goddess Kaliamman, tracing to an 1860 shrine near Orchard Road and rebuilt at Toa Payoh in 1982 (consecrated 1986). Notable for founding Saraswathi Kindergarten, said to be Singapore's first pre-school, and a stop on the Toa Payoh Heritage Trail's 'Of Faiths & Beliefs' route.

Singapore's first sensory park (opened 2009), a 1.1-hectare garden by Surbana and Yoshisuke Miyake split into five zones for sight, smell, touch, sound and taste — with larger-than-life optical-illusion mirrors that reveal a hidden face, resonating steel 'drum' plates, a playground and a fragrant garden.

Inaugurated 7 Feb 1974, the second public library of the 1970s branch-building drive and a civic anchor of the town — its Children's Section riffs on the iconic dragon playground with hexagonal mosaic-tile motifs. A pioneering heartland library documented in NLB's BiblioAsia.
sights.k: Free; closed Mondays historically — check hours

sights.n: Toa Payoh Seu Teck Sean Tong
sights.address: 15 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh (Kampong Hup Choon Hng site), Singapore
sights.w: A Chinese charitable temple established as an attap hut in 1942 and rebuilt 1959, enshrining the deity Song Da Feng and blending Buddhist, Taoist and Confucian rites. Its medical wing (opened 1967) still gives free Traditional Chinese Medicine consultations — a living community institution on the heritage trail.

sights.address: Toa Payoh MRT Station (NS19), 480 Lorong 6 Toa Payoh, Singapore
sights.w: A station wall mural in SMRT's heritage-mural series telling Toa Payoh's story as the first town wholly designed and built by the HDB — co-created by James Suresh, better known as co-creator of the 'Mr Kiasu' comics. A quick, free public-art stop right at the interchange.

The town's big community-and-sports clubhouse (open to the public, not just NSmen) with a leisure pool and lap lanes, bowling, badminton, tennis, gym, karaoke and F&B — the recreation hub that carries on locally while the adjacent old stadium and swimming complex are redeveloped into the Toa Payoh Integrated Development.
